tasks.title: Transit of Venus
tasks.statement: Recently, on June 6, 2012, an infrequent astronomical phenomenon, transit of Venus across the solar disc, took place. The next transit of Venus will take place only in 2117. Calculate the date of that transit. (Answer without calculations will not be considered even as a partial solution.)

parts.question: Calculate the date of the next transit of Venus.
parts.reference: To calculate next inferior conjunctions we need first to find the synodic period Ts of Venus: Ts = Te * Tv / (Te - Tv) = 583.92 days. January 1, 2117 will be 38194 days after June 6, 2012. December 31, 2017 [2117], respectively, will be 38558 days after that date. 38194 / 583.92 = 65.41; 38558 / 583.92 = 66.03. It means that the close approach of Venus in 2117 will be after 66 synodic periods of Venus: 66 * 583.92 = 38538.7. 38538 days are 20 days earlier than the date 38558 that we calculated for December 31, 2117. Thus, 38538 days after June 6, 2012 corresponds to December 11, 2117. Answer: The next transit of Venus will take place on December 11, 2117.

tasks.title: Transit of Pseudovenus
tasks.statement: Recently, on June 6, 2012, an infrequent astronomical phenomenon, transit of Venus across the solar disc took place. Suppose somebody did not understand the phenomenon and ascribed it not to transit of real Venus but of some moon, which we name Pseudovenus, rotating around the Earth in a circular orbit. Find the radius of the orbit of Pseudovenus and diameter of this sky body. Effects due to axial rotating of the Earth should not be taken into account.

parts.question: Find the radius of the orbit of Pseudovenus and diameter of this sky body.
parts.reference: Visible motion of Venus depends on the synodic motion of the planet. The synodic angular speed is u = (omega_V - omega_E) * R_V / (R_E - R_V). For Pseudovenus rotating around the Earth, u = omega_P + omega_E. Using third Kepler law and relations, Rp = [GM_E * (R_E - R_V)^2 / (4 * pi^2 * (R_V/T_V - R_E/T_E))^2]^(1/3) = 2.92 * 10^6 m = 2.92 mln km (or using Moon comparison Rp = 7.62 Ru = 2.93 mln km). Size of Pseudovenus: rp = r_V * Rp / (R_E - R_V) = 8.55 * 10^5 m = 850 km (approx. 0.25 diameters of the Moon). Note: Additional point may be given for the students who note that this distance is out of the Hill sphere for the Earth and so this situation is impossible.

tasks.title: Old persons’ star
tasks.statement: There is ancient legend in Korea that says, if you managed to see the “Old persons’ star” thrice, you are lucky person and will live a long life. The “Old persons’ star”, now known as Canopus, was seen brighter and better in past times, but even now sometimes one can see this star in Korea. Estimate approximately what visible stellar magnitude Canopus may have when observing it from the southern coast of Jeju island (Korea) in the most favorable conditions. The territory of the island is located at latitudes between 33°12'N and 33°34'N and longitudes between 126°09' E and 126°57' E. Take from the tables and recollect for yourself the necessary additional information.

parts.question: Estimate approximately what visible stellar magnitude Canopus may have when observing it from the southern coast of Jeju island in the most favorable conditions.
parts.reference: Latitude of the southern point is 33°12'N. Canopus culminates at altitude h = 90° - phi + delta = 90° - 33°12' + (-52°42') = 4°06'. Atmospheric absorption: 1 / sin(4°06') = 14. Additional absorption of light at 4°06' is (1 / sin(4°06') - 1) = 13 times more than in zenith. Delta m = 0.23 * (1 / sin(4°06') - 1) = 3.0m. m_v = m_0 + Delta m = -0.72 + 3.0 = 2.3m. Reasonable answers are from 1.5 to 4.

tasks.title: Stars on Mars
tasks.statement: As you know, last year the Polar Bear (whom you have already met in the texts of many International Astronomy Olympiads) arrived to Mars for astronomical observations. Nowadays his friend Penguin also made a fascinating journey to Mars. At the same instant of time, the Bear and the Penguin observe stars in zenith and see Canopus and Sirius respectively. Estimate roughly, what is the distance (measured on the Martian surface) between the animals? At what height above the horizon does the Bear observe Sirius? The solution has to include a picture with an image of the Bear and the Penguin on Mars. Necessary sizes or angular sizes should be in the picture. Recollect for yourself the necessary information about the Polar Bear and Penguin.

parts.question: Estimate roughly, what is the distance between the animals and at what height above the horizon does the Bear observe Sirius, including a picture with the Bear and Penguin on Mars.
parts.reference: Canopus and Sirius have almost the same RA while the difference in DEC is significant. Beta = delta_1 - delta_2 = (-16°42'58") - (-52°41'45") = 35°59' = 36°. Distance along Martian surface = Beta(°)*pi*R/180 = 2130 km (or ~2300 km), where R = 3397 km. Height of Sirius for the Bear: h = 90° - Beta = 90° - 36° = 54°. Picture should show the Bear and Penguin on Mars with necessary sizes or angular sizes.

tasks.title: Venus and Earth
tasks.statement: At what maximum distance from the Venus ecliptic the Earth can be visible in the sky from Venus (actually, from a point ouside the Venus atmosphere)? Orbits of the planets may be considered circular.

parts.question: Find the maximum distance from the Venus ecliptic the Earth can be visible in the sky from Venus, and estimate the stellar magnitude of the Earth in this situation.
parts.reference: Maximum space distance from Earth to Venus ecliptic is H = R_E * sin(i) = 1 AU * sin(3.4°) = 0.0593 AU, where i = 3.4°. In Venusian sky, minimum distance in opposition is L = R_E - R_V = 1 AU - 0.723 AU = 0.277 AU. Maximum distance angle Beta from equation H = L * tan(Beta), tg(Beta) = 0.0593 / 0.277 = 0.214, Beta = 12.1°. Stellar magnitude estimate: Compare with Mars visible from Earth in opposition. F_E/F_M = (alpha_E/alpha_M) * (D_E/D_M)^2 * (R_M - R_Sun)^2 / (R_E - R_V)^2 = (0.36/0.15) * (12756/6794)^2 * (0.524 * 1.524)^2 / (0.277^2 * 1) = 70. Delta m = -2.5 * lg(70) = -4.6. Stellar magnitude of the Earth m = -2.0 + Delta m = -6.6m.

tasks.title: Parallaxes
tasks.statement: In our part of the Galaxy the mean distance between the stars is about 6 light years. Assume that an interferometer can measure parallaxes with an error of +-0.001 arc second. How many stars of our Galaxy could have their parallax determined by this interferometer?

parts.question: How many stars of our Galaxy could have their parallax determined by this interferometer?
parts.reference: 6 light years = 1.84 pc. Parallax of 0.001" corresponds to 1000 pc. Uniform distribution sphere: N = 4*pi/3 * (1000/1.84)^3 = 6.7 * 10^8 (or 7 * 10^8). Considering Galaxy thickness (about 400 pc), volume is a cylinder with radius 1000 pc and height 400 pc. N = pi * (1000/1.84)^2 * (400/1.84) = 2 * 10^8 (two hundred million stars). Understanding that the thickness of the Galaxy should be taken into account is most important.
